introduction: Video excerpt from The History of the Crusades video

vocabulary.definition: a journey or voyage undertaken by a group of people with a particular purpose, especially that of exploration, scientific research, or war.
vocabulary.example: The expedition to the Arctic was led by a team of experienced explorers.

vocabulary.definition: a military operation in which enemy forces surround a town or building, cutting off essential supplies, with the aim of compelling the surrender of those inside.
vocabulary.example: The castle was under siege for months before finally falling to the invaders.

vocabulary.definition: to rob a place using violence, especially in wartime.
vocabulary.example: The invading army proceeded to pillage the village, taking everything of value.

vocabulary.definition: adhering to the traditional and established faith, especially in religion.
vocabulary.example: The Orthodox community celebrated Easter according to their ancient customs.

vocabulary.definition: to take apart or demolish (a structure or machine).
vocabulary.example: The old factory was dismantled to make space for a new shopping mall.

vocabulary.definition: a medieval crusader state established by the leaders of the Fourth Crusade in Constantinople.
vocabulary.example: The Latin Empire was short-lived, lasting from 1204 to 1261 in Byzantine territories.
